The rule: for each 3x3 all-black neighborhood (centered at r,c), fill it with 1 (dark blue). Note the verifier does one pass over original out but modifies out as it goes; but since it checks neighborhood_total on the current out (which may have been modified), filling creates 1s not 0s, so subsequent checks are unaffected (1 is nonzero). So effectively find all 3x3 all-zero blocks and fill with 1s. Overlapping blocks would just merge; but since after filling, neighborhood_total nonzero, it skips. So only non-overlapping detected in scan order.

But careful: scan order matters — after filling a block, later blocks that overlap would be skipped. But since filled cells are 1 (nonzero), any block containing a filled cell won't be all-zero anyway. So actually it's just: union of all 3x3 all-zero blocks in the original grid, filled with 1. Wait, because a block that overlaps a filled region would have a 1 in it, so it wouldn't be all-zero originally either. Since the original block must be all-zero, and filled cells come from all-zero blocks, any block that gets skipped is one containing a filled cell — but that block also originally contained 0 there (since filled cell was 0 originally). Hmm, so it could originally be all-zero but get skipped due to overlap.

Example: block A at (r,c) all-zero, block B at (r,c+1) all-zero overlapping. Then after filling A, B's neighborhood contains 1s, skipped. So the result is not the union of all all-zero blocks. It's greedy scan order.
